outcome: No change: as of September 2026, Rule 110 (Cook, proved 2004, published 2004/2009) remains the only one of the 88 unique elementary cellular automata directly proven Turing complete (with Rule 124, its reflection, following as a corollary); Rule 54 remains conjectured but unproven; no source published after 26 January 2024 reports a new proof, disproof, or completed classification covering the Turing-completeness status of the remaining rules.
summary: This bullet asks for the Turing-completeness status of all 88 unique elementary cellular automata (ECA) — effectively a request for a complete classification, of which currently only one data point (Rule 110, proved Turing complete by Matthew Cook in 2004, with Rule 124 following by reflection symmetry) is settled, and one other (Rule 54) is a long-standing conjecture with no proof either way. I searched broadly for any 2024–2026 work that proves or disproves universality for any additional specific ECA rule, or that advances a systematic classification of all 88 rules' computational status, and found none. Several tangentially related papers turned up: an ICLR 2025 paper ('Intelligence at the Edge of Chaos') that pretrains GPT-2 on ECA-generated data to study emergent intelligence — it treats Rule 110's Turing completeness only as background context and does not touch the classification question; a 2026 ResearchGate/preprint paper ('Toward Automated Identification of Turing-Complete Cellular Automata via Structural and Complexity Analysis') that proposes a quantitative 'Complexity Score' and 'Behavioral Index' framework to flag *candidate* rules likely to be Turing complete, but explicitly stops short of proving Turing completeness for any specific rule — it is a screening heuristic, not a resolution; and a 2026 paper on Rule 22 as an algebraic reference point for Rule 30, which is about algebraic structure, not universality. None of these change what a careful reader would write in this bullet's entry: the status of the 86 remaining unique rules (all but Rule 110/124) is exactly as unresolved as it was in January 2024, and no AI system produced, checked, or contributed to any actual proof or disproof of universality for any of these rules. The record is `open` with `no_change_found` true.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2026 'automated identification' framework paper constitutes 'progress' in a loose sense, since it is new work aimed at the classification question and could plausibly be seen as narrowing where computational universality might be found. But per §3.1, a record/search-style narrowing only counts when the record IS the question; here the underlying existence question (is rule X Turing complete?) is not answered by a complexity-score heuristic that only ranks candidates, so I classified this as no change rather than `progress`. If the paper's rule rankings were later used to drive an actual proof, that would change the classification, but no such follow-up was found.
what_would_settle_it: A peer-reviewed or well-digested preprint proving or disproving Turing completeness for a specific ECA rule other than 110/124, or a completed systematic classification (proof or disproof) covering the computational status of all 88 unique rules, dated after 26 January 2024.
